$Comment: What a player sees when they put on another piece of a gear set and no tier of it comes on or
goes off: one quiet line with the set's name and how far along it is, and no sound. A piece
that does change a tier is Gear_Set_Tier's notice instead, which carries the same count. It
fires only for a real change: logging in or changing worlds with pieces on says nothing, and
neither does taking a piece off.
This is the library's own neutral default. A mod that ships a file with this same name in its
own pack replaces it, and a server owner can do the same from the owner layer.
The moment carries 'set' (the set id, also under 'source', so each set keeps ONE line that
the next piece rewrites instead of adding another under it), 'name' (what the set is called,
in the reader's language), 'pieces' (how many distinct members the player has on, never more
than 'total'), 'total' (how many pieces the full set takes, read from its tiers; once the count
stands there, a spare piece says nothing more), 'next' (the line of the first tier
the player has still to earn, in the reader's language; absent when every tier holds or that
tier authors no Text) and 'hasnext' (true when 'next' is there). 'player' is always the name
To show what the next tier gives under the count, add a Secondary reading 'next'. Add a Sound
group to give each piece a click.
